text:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — do we aim for a minimal profile surface (preset IDs + a couple flags) or a fully expressive profile DSL? Trying to balance runtime simplicity, ops debuggability, and customer flexibility. See RFC link: https://go/repo/rfc-precision-profiles

Alex: +1 to minimal. Ops already spends too much time chasing weird combos. :raised_hands:

Sam: Minimal is simpler but we lose some important axes (per-model calibration: kvcache policies, attn-fusion hints). Those actually change quality noticeably for some models.

Rui: Middle ground proposal: two-layer surface — canonical core_profiles (hosted presets: high_quality, balanced, low_cost) + a small overrides whitelist. Overrides are validated and restricted to safe knobs. Runtime consumes profile_id and a prevalidated override token.

Alex: How do we validate overrides without adding latency per request? Per-request validation hop will kill p50.

Rui: Validation is async/cacheable. Validator service compiles an override into a signed compiled_profile_id. Runtime only looks up compiled_profile_id in local cache. Pseudocode:
```
# request path
compiled = cache.get(compiled_profile_key)
if not compiled:
  compiled = validator.fetch(compiled_profile_key)  # rare
apply(compiled)
```
Cache TTLs + prewarm on deploys.

Maya: Ops concerns: telemetry cardinality. If every customer creates many override permutations we lose visibility. Need limits and aggregation dimensions (profile_template, safety_level, quant_strategy).

Sam: Also require deterministic fallback: if compiled profile fails or violates safety, runtime must fallback to a same-safety_level canonical profile (no retrying random overrides).

oncall-bot: NOTE: canary created: canary/precision-profile-surface -> 5% traffic for 24h. See incident runbook link.

Alex: Security & privacy question: do we allow customer overrides for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)? Maybe only opt-in via contract.

Maya: Good point. Suggest default: Hosted = allowed with whitelist, Dedicated = allowed with extra review, Private = disabled unless explicitly enabled by SRE/security.

Maya: Action items before RFC follow-up: (1) Draft whitelist of allowed override knobs (2) Define telemetry signals + alert thresholds (degscore, per-profile token cost, rollback rate) (3) Sketch Validator API and cache semantics (4) Canary + ops playbook. Volunteers?

Rui: I'll take (3) and start a concrete API sketch + a small PoC for compiled_profile tokens.

Sam: I'll own (2) telemetry metrics and build a dashboard template + alert rules.

Alex: I'll coordinate (4) canary plan and ops rollbacks, and help with (1) whitelist scoping.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll assemble a short RFC follow-up with these decisions and ping legal/SRE for Private deployment gating. Will also add a short example of the compiled_profile token format. :sparkles:
